```{python}
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
import _dpm as dpm

con = dpm.connect()
known = dpm.releases(con)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(
    "One page per reporting template, generated from the EBA's DPM 2.0 database: what the "
    "template is, what it breaks down by, what checks it, and what has changed about it "
    f"since DPM {known[0]['code']}.\n"
)
print(
    f"This build read a database carrying {len(known)} releases — "
    + ", ".join(release["code"] for release in known)
    + ".\n"
)
```

It is for whoever has to fill a template in and wants to know what a cell means, whether
the rule that will reject their file is still switched on, and whether the column they
have been keying a time series on has always meant the same thing.

## Two things worth knowing before you read a page

**A datapoint is not its coordinate.** The DPM has two reference systems: `VariableID`,
which is the identity of a datapoint, and the table coordinate — template, row, column,
sheet — which is where that datapoint sits in one version of one template. Within a
version the coordinate is unambiguous. Across releases it is not: coordinates have been
reused for different datapoints. If you key a time series on `r0550_c0020`, you are
keying on an address, not on a thing.

**Nobody wrote the descriptions.** Every description you will see is composed from the
template name, the row label and the column label, because the model holds no sentence
for a datapoint. This is not a shortcut taken here; it is what the model contains.
